conflicts.description: Codex recorded release gates R4-R8 as passed on the strength of a hosted proof that built its own sources in code; Claude contested that the gates could be passed on evidence the proof generated for itself. The owner ruled that the hosted proof be wired to the real restored corpus with the synthetic fallback removed.
conflicts.contestedAction: Recording R4 through R8 as passed in governingDocuments/scientific-learning-release-status.json on the basis of a hosted proof whose sources were constructed in code rather than read from the real corpus.
conflicts.rationaleSummary: Two agents worked the same gates concurrently. Codex built the GitHub-hosted encrypted state boundary, the private Crucible-Learning-State repository, and migrated the real 221.69 MiB encrypted extraction queue - all genuine infrastructure - then marked R4-R8 passed using src/hostedLearningProof.js. Claude, reviewing that commit, found the hosted proof built its two independent sources in code from the claim string itself, superseded a candidate it generated for itself and labelled a repository test fixture, exercised the R8 safety cases against a stubbed fetch, and never referenced the restored real corpus at all. R4 requires at least one real source and R8 requires live cases, so the recorded gate states and the release plan's own requirements could not both be true. Claude froze its own competing implementation of the same file rather than overwrite Codex's, and escalated to the owner.
evidence: src/hostedLearningProof.js at 53c2694 built its R4 sources in code: sources=[{sourceId:'https://proof.example.edu/arrays',content:`Array reference. ${CLAIM}`},{sourceId:'https://proof.example.org/arrays',content:`Independent array guide. ${CLAIM}`}] - the claim string with a prefix, from hostnames that resolve to nothing.
The R7 supersession candidate was self-generated with provenance sourceType:'github-hosted-proof', sourceId:`github-run:${runId}`, license:'repository test fixture'.
The R8 safety cases ran against fetchImpl:async()=>response(body,type), a stub, while the release plan requires live kill-switch, duplicate, injection, executable, and blocked-source cases.
grep for the restored corpus inside src/hostedLearningProof.js returned 0 matches: the 221.69 MiB queue migrated to Crucible-Learning-State was never read by the proof that marked the gates passed.

governingDocuments/scientific-learning-release-status.json recorded R4=passed-hosted-project-bound-proof through R8=passed-hosted-combined-live-safety-cycle while the same record left R2's live drain and R3's discovery run open, so no real source had been processed.
Both agents independently created src/hostedLearningProof.js and test/hostedLearningProof.test.js with different designs, a direct filename collision on concurrent work.

sides.instruction: Record R4-R8 as passed on the strength of a GitHub-hosted run that exercises the full pipeline end to end with encrypted, restart-safe, project-bound durable state.

sides.source: governingDocuments/scientific-learning-release-plan.md, gates R4 and R8 and the non-negotiable boundaries
sides.instruction: R4 requires at least one real source through retrieval, provenance hashing, bounded extraction, deduplication, and candidate custody; R8 requires live safety and deduplication cases; and no one-off success, retrieval, or repetition is proof.
Do not mark a gate passed on data the proof generated for itself. Either wire the hosted proof to the real restored corpus, or return R4-R8 to pending.

alternatives: Revert the R4-R8 gate markings to pending and leave the hosted proof unchanged, preserving the infrastructure while withdrawing the unsupported claims.
Wire the hosted proof to the real restored corpus, remove the fixture fallback entirely, and let the gates be earned or fail closed on real data.
Leave the markings and the proof as they are, and record the fixture basis openly in the release status so nothing downstream mistakes them for real learning.

resolution.decision: Wire the hosted proof to the real restored corpus and remove the synthetic fallback entirely, so R4-R6 are learned from real extracted sources or the run fails closed with the gates reported unsatisfied. The owner directed this in session on 2026-08-31 with 'I want a real learning machine so wire it up triple check it works'.
resolution.rationaleSummary: The infrastructure Codex built is sound and was kept; only the fixture basis for the gate claims was replaced. Joining the real corpus to evaluation also required fixing a structural defect that had made real learning impossible: routeThreeWayComparison decided shared scope by comparing claimBoundary, which extraction builds from the source document, so two independent real sources never matched and every real pair routed to bounded-scope-or-version-update instead of new-claim-evaluation. An optional claimScope now carries the declared tested scope separately from provenance, is never inferred, and leaves candidates without one behaving exactly as before. R7's supersession and R8's safety cases remain fixture-based and are recorded as such rather than claimed as real.
